rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT II 4；Mr. John Eyres 另立五命题法（Caroline Tables 求相位纬度）亦录于本章，Morinus 反对二圆取相之说

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.original_text: In Directing the Ascendant, or Horoscope, you are to perform your Operations by Oblique Ascentions only, taken under the Latitude of the place of Birth... find also the Oblique Ascention of your Promittor (with Latitude, if he have any) under the same Elevation of the Pole aforesaid: and lastly Substract the Oblique Ascention of your Significator (viz. Ascendant) from the Oblique Ascention of your Promittor (viz. the Body, or Aspect of a planet) and the remainer is the Ark of Direction required. See the 25th Aph. of Ptol. Centiloq. In Directing of the Meridian Circle, (viz. the M.C. I.C. or Cusps of the tenth, or fourth Houses) that is alwayes performed by Right Ascentions. Thus, Substract the R.A. of the M.C. or I.C. from the R.A. Of your Promittor, (alwayes regarding his Latitude) and the remainer is the Ark of Direction sought.
rules.translation: 方向操作三法：①升点/天宫之方向——只用斜升，于出生地纬度下求 Promittor（有纬则计）之斜升，减升点之斜升，余即方向弧（Ptolemy Centiloquium 第25格言）；②MC/IC（10/4宫头）之方向——恒用赤经，Promittor 之赤经（计纬度）减 MC/IC 之赤经，余即方向弧。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT III 1-2；7宫（西角）及四角宫头之法同升点；升点之法见 Ptolemy Centiloq. Aph.25

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 六步求位置圈极→斜升/斜降差
rules.original_text: To Direct the Sun, Moon, and Part of Fortune, you are to observe another Method (viz.) The Elevation of the Pole above the Circles of Position they are upon must first be obtained, provided they are not posited upon the first Cusp of some of the Houses; for then you have it given without farther trouble. The Rule is as followeth. First, Having the Planets Longitude, and Latitude. Secondly, Find his Declination North, or South. Thirdly, His Right Ascention. Fourthly, By that his distance from the Meridian, (viz. The tenth, or fourth House, according as he is plac'd under, or, above the Earth.) Fifthly, By that the Poles Elevation above the Circle of Position. Sixthly, His Oblique Ascention under that Pole, if posited in the tenth, eleventh, twelfth, first, second, or third Houses; or Oblique Descention, if posited in the fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, or ninth Houses.
rules.translation: 日月与福点之方向（Pole of Position 法）：先求其所在位置圈之地极高度——六步：①星之黄经黄纬；②求南北赤纬；③求赤经；④由此求其距子午线（依在地平上下取10或4宫）；⑤由此求其位置圈之极高；⑥在该极下取斜升（星落10/11/12/1/2/3宫时）或斜降（落4/5/6/7/8/9宫时）。再求 Promittor 同极下之斜升，相减得方向弧；其余诸星作 Significator 时同法。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT III 3；亦可用星之对宫位以斜升代之

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 依星性与本命强弱定方向效验
rules.original_text: In Directing the Ascendant, or Horoscope, you are to perform your Operations by Oblique Ascentions only, taken under the Latitude of the place of Birth... In Directing of the Meridian Circle, (viz. the M.C. I.C. or Cusps of the tenth, or fourth Houses) that is alwayes performed by Right Ascentions.
rules.translation: 方向效力总论：术者须知行星之本性及其在本命之偶然所主（所落宫、所主宫、强弱），察方向之吉凶与 Promittor 在本命之强弱（Radix 中如何固强或受损），据以裁断方向之征应。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT IV 1-2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 强弱与落位定吉凶程度
rules.original_text: If the Significator, and Promissor were both strong in the Radix, and the Direction falls in a good place of the Figure, or in their Dignities, and it be also a good Direction, (viz.) To the Conjunction, Sextile, or Trine of some Benevolent Planet, &c. Then you may conclude the Effects thereof will be very Famous to the Native. But on the other side, if the Significator, and Promittor, were both weak in the Radix, and the Direction fall in their Debilities, Judge the contrary; or if a Significator, and Promittor were but meanly Fortified in the Radix, and the Direction happen to be good, and fall well; the Native may not expect that the Accidents signified thereby should take place so effectually... a good Direction brings much Prosperity, and Happiness, along with it, to the Native; and it will be of the same kind that the Significator doth properly denote of himself, consideration had to the House he governs in the Radix... The Promissors signification is also to be consulted, which intimates the cause of the happiness that is promised.
rules.translation: 方向吉凶裁断：Significator 与 Promissor 本命皆强、方向落图之吉位或其尊贵处、且为吉方向（吉星之合/六合/三合）=效果显赫大吉；二者皆弱、方向落其失势处=反断；中平则效验减半。吉方向所许之福=Significator 本性所主之福（参其在 Radix 所主之宫）；Promissor 之征示其福之由来。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT IV 3-4；并察方向所落之星座与天宫、届时二星之强弱、行运照临等；一切方向须合命主年龄

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 升=命体、MC=荣位母、日=荣身父、月=体质婚妻、福点=财
rules.original_text: The Ascendant, or Horoscope, which signifies the Life of any Person in his Nativity; as also his Body, Complexion, Manners, and Affection of the Mind, is therefore Directed to his several Promittors; which if it meets with good Directions, and the Aspects, or Bodies of fortunate Planets, it denotes health, prosperity, and happiness... But on the contrary, if the Ascendant meete with bad Directions, viz. the Bodies, or Beams of the Malevolent Planets (or Stars) which accidentally govern evil houses in the Radix; then this Direction portends much Mischief, Sickness, or other Infirmities, or Crosses... The M.C. or Mid-heaven is directed for Preferment, Honour, Offices, Friendship from Great Persons, Trade, or Profession, also for Accidents to the Mother of the Native. The Sun is directed for Honour, and Preferment, be it publique, or private; for Friendship, and Favour from Persons in power; and more particular it is Directed for Accidents relating to the Body, as the Health, or Sickness of the Native. The Direction of the Sun points out many things relating to the Estate, and Condition of the Natives Father also. The Moon is Directed... she signifies the Constitution, and Complexion; as also the Inclination, and Intentions of the Native, the Natives Journeys, long, or short, Marriage; and in particular, the Estate, and Condition of the Wife; Women in general, and all near Relations. The Part of Fortune is Directed for Profit, and Increase, or loss of Estate, according as it meets with the Aspects, or Conjunctions of good, or bad Planets.
rules.translation: 各 Hylegiacal 应征星所主：升点=寿命/身体/体质/品性/心意，遇吉方向=康泰幸福、遇凶星体或恶照（尤本命主凶宫之星）=病患灾厄（依克星之性）；MC=荣位、贵人之谊、职业，及母之事故；太阳=公私荣进、权贵之谊、身体健康疾病、父之身家状况；月亮=体质禀赋、意向、远近行旅、婚姻、妻之身家、女性及诸近亲；福点=财之增减（随所遇吉凶星之合相）。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT IV 6-10；Coley 以为以 MC 方向断身病不当（除非光荣之死如斩首等）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 依各星本性定方向之征
rules.original_text: First Saturn is Directed, to signifie the Fruits of the Earth, Inheritances, Possessions, Buildings, &c. Fears, and Jealousies, &c. And this according to their strength, or weakness of Saturn in the Nativity. Jupiter is Directed for Wealth, Prosperity, Advancement, etc. Children in general, Wisdome, Prudence, Temperance, &c. Mars is Directed for Courage, and boldness of Spirit, viz. Animosity, Victory, War, Contentions, and Law-Suits, as also the Estate, and Condition of Brethren. Venus is Directed for all kind of Pleasures, and Delights, Love, Matrimony, Costly Ornaments, &c. and for the female Sex in general. Mercury is Directed for Learning, Ingenuity, the Understanding; as also for Merchandizing, and Trade, Industry, Journeys, &c. Lastly, for younger Brethren.
rules.translation: 诸行星作 Significator 方向之所主：土=地产、承继、产业、营造、忧惧忌妒（按土在本命之强弱）；木=财富、亨通、进身、子女、智慧、节制；火=勇气胆量、争胜、战争、争讼、兄弟之身家；金=诸般逸乐、爱情、婚姻、华饰、女性；水=学问、巧智、理解、商贾、勤业、行旅、幼弟。皆按其本命所落之宫与所主之宫酌断。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT IV 11-12

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.original_text: If you would know how long the force of a Direction shall continue, you are to consider the strength, or weakness both of Significator, and Promittor in the Geniture, if there beth strong, or essentially dignified therein, the effects of the Direction shall powerfully manifest itself; and whatever is promised thereby, shall take place effectually and continue durable, until such time the as the Significator or some other, meets with another Promittor. But if they are weak in the Radix, the effects of the Direction will be inconsiderable. Observe also that if the Infortunate Planets happen to be Promissors in any Direction, and therein threaten some eminent danger unto the Native; this evil will not afflict the Native, and take place to the height, if so be they were strong, and Potent in the Radix. But if they were debilitated there, you may expect the greater infelicity. 'tis also to be observed that Jupiter, and Venus may accidentally happen to be Infortunes; and Saturn, and Mars, Fortunes in some Mens Genitures, according to the Houses they govern, or their Position in the figure. If two Directions happen to be in force together... consider which of them is the strongest, and to which the Revolution of the Year doth best agree, and Judge that Direction will operate forcibly; which if it be the good Direction, it will much mittigate (if not quite extinguish) the effects of the bad; or if the bad Direction, 'twill overpower the force of the good one.
rules.translation: 方向力之久暂与吉凶参决：二星本命强或有本然尊贵=其效果力显且持久（直至 Significator 再遇他 Promittor）；弱则效微。凶星为 Promittor 而本命强=所危不致全发；本命弱=祸尤烈。木金偶可为凶、土火偶可为吉（视其所主之宫与盘中位置）。二方向同时并作：取强者、与当年流年 Revolution 最合者断其力——吉者缓（或灭）凶者，凶者压吉者。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIII SECT IV 13-16；Coley 自云此处不拟详列方向效果，荐读 Lilly《Introduction》

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 效力=Significator 与 Promittor 相合
rules.original_text: CHAP. XXIV. OF DIRECTIONS IN NATIVITIES, AND THEIR EFFECTS, ACCORDING TO MORINUS. Since 'tis certain that the Term of Directions, i.e. the places of the Significators, and Promittors are fixed, in the Primum Mobile... and that the effect of a Direction is neither from the Significator, or Promittor alone, but from both concurring. First, The several Cusps of the Houses, the Planets, and Aspects at the Moment of Birth, are actually determined to some particular thing in respect of the Native, but potentially to divers other things; so Saturn in the first House is actually determined to the Natives temperament, health, manners, ingenuity, &c. But potentially to all Accidents represented by other Houses respectively. Secondly, That the influx of the Coelestial Figure at the Moment of Birth is impressed on the sensible part of the Native, not confusedly, but distinctly... so that the Coelestial Figure is not only the external Principle of Life to the Native, but likewise the efficient Cause of a like internal Principle in the Native. Thirdly, That every Significator in the Figure of Heaven, whether Planet, or Cusp, Ruling by its Vertue, as well essential, as accidental in the Native, by imprinting his Character, is some Principle of Life, Action, Marriage, or Passion; to which, by a potential Determination, the other parts of the Figure are referred; so that such things will happen concerning that Principle, as the said places are naturally, or accidentally determined unto, and in the same order of time, as is the distance of those places from such Principals, so as the nearest will soon be brought out of Power into Act, i.e. will first produce its effect.
rules.translation: Morinus《Astrologia Gallica》方向论（CHAP XXIV）要点：方向之效非独出 Significator 或 Promittor，乃二者相合而生。①生时宫头、行星与相位对命主实际已定于某些事，而潜能地定于诸他事（如土星在1宫实定于体质健康品性，而潜能及于12宫等所表诸事）。②生时天图之灌入非混淆而是清晰地印于命主觉受之部——天图不但为命主生命之外在原理，亦为其内在相似原理之效因（天地与命主在行与受之间相契之故）。③每一 Significator（行星或宫头）以其本然+偶然之力印其性格于命主，为生命/行事/婚姻/情欲之某原理，图中他部潜能地系属之——其发生依诸位距此原理之远近为序，近者先由潜能入于现实。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIV 1-3

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 效以周年周转入实、或先或后
rules.original_text: Fourthly, That since the Coelestial Figure at Birth is a thing stable, and permanent, wherein casually, and implicitely is contained the whole Life of the Native, with his Accidents... there must be some cause in Heaven thereof, which can be no other than the succession, and order of the Promittors potentially determined... the Planets, and their Aspects are to be reduced from this potential Determination into Act, which is done by the first Revolution of the first Heaven that begins at the Moment of Birth; for whilst by such Natural Revolution every Promittor is brought to the Circle of Position, which each Significator possessed at that Moment of Birth, the same is actually determined to produce an effect at some time. Fifthly, Now the effects of a Direction cannot be produced at the very Moment of the Nativity, because then the Promittor is not actually in the place of the Significator, but only potentially; and therefore its effects afterwards brought into Act by successive Motion, about so many Years from the Genesis, as the Promittor is distant in Degrees of the Aequator from the Circle of Position of the Significator. Sixthly, That though the Terms of Directions remain fix'd, and unmoveable in the Heavens, yet their effects may be produced on Earth, viz. in Man, because by the Radical Influx... after so many annual Revolutions of the Sun, as the Ark of Direction contains of his Diurnal ones... the effects not alwayes happen precizely at the time signified by the Ark of Direction, but are sometimes hastned, or retarded, and fall out before, or after it.
rules.translation: Morinus 论（续）：④生时天图为恒久之物、含蓄命主一生诸事——天上必有主其序之因，即潜能确定之 Promittor 之相继与次序；潜能入实由生时起之第一天之第一周转（Revolution）完成——Promittor 被带至生时 Significator 所在之位置圈时即实定于届时生效。⑤方向之效不能在生时即生（Promittor 彼时仅潜能地在 Significator 之位），须经连续之动于距生约若干年（=Promittor 距 Significator 位置圈之赤道度数）方成。⑥方向之限虽在天恒久不动，其效缘生时之根本灌入与日后太阳周年周转可成于人身——效不精确应于方向弧所标之时，常有或先或后之速缓。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIV 4-6；且须周年/月周 Revolution 与行运之实际参合

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.original_text: Seventhly, A Significator is nothing but a Coelestial substance, i.e. a part of Heaven, or a Planet signifying of it self, by reason of its Determination, concerning some kind of Accidents of a Native; whence it is also said to be the Significator of such a kind of Accident, so far as the same is to be effected by the Direction. Hence it appears there are so many Significators for Directions, as there are Planets, and Houses, to which if we add the Part of Fortune, there will be twenty in all. Eighthly, But note by Planets we mean not the Bodies of the Planets, but their fixed places in the Primo Mobile, or those parts of the Primum Mobile, determined to the nature of the said Planets at Moment of Birth; note farther, that each Planet may have as many significations as it hath wayes to be determined concerning the Native, as being in one House, and Lord of another. Ninthly, A Promissor is a part of the Primum Mobile, determined concerning some certain kind of those Accidents happening to a Native, or the second Term of a Direction, as it by it self presages something to come concerning any thing represented by the Significator.
rules.translation: Morinus 论（续）：⑦Significator=天体（天之一部或行星），因其确定之故自征命主某类事故——方向 Significator 共二十：七行星+十二宫头+福点。⑧所谓行星非指其体，乃其在原动天中于生时被定于该星之性之固定位；一星可因落一宫又主一宫而有数重征义、须为诸事分别方向。⑨Promissor=原动天之一部、定于命主某类事故者，即方向之第二端，自征其所许于 Significator 所表之事。
rules.notes: CHAP XXIV 7-9

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: Ptolemy=度年；Maginus=视赤经差；Naibod=平运动（今通行）
rules.original_text: CHAP. XXV. OF THE MEASURE OF TIME IN DIRECTIONS. Ptolomy's Measure is for every degree of the Aequator, to allow one year, and for every minute 6 dayes, 2 hours 6 minutes. And so 365 dayes, 6 hours contain one whole degree, or 60 minutes. II) Then Antonius Maginus... affirms that the Measure of Time ought to be taken from the true, and apparent Motion of the Sun, and not his simple Motion... the difference between the Sun's Right Ascention at the Birth, and at the same hour, and minute the next day following, shall be the Measure of Time for a Year. III) But a third Measure of Time (and now generally approved of as best) is that of Valentine Naibod... grounded upon the Sun's mean Motion, to be the measure of Time for a Year. And by that Rule one whole degree gives one year, 5 dayes, 8 hours, and 59 minutes, 8 seconds gives one compleat Year, and so every minute gives 6 dayes, and about 4 hours. IV) This last Measure is by all Modern Authors approved as the best... Now there is no considerable difference in any of those Measures of Time, and either of them may be indifferently used.
rules.translation: 方向时间度量三法：①Ptolemy 法：赤道每度=一年，每分=6日2时6分（365日6时=1度=60分）——通行至上一世纪无争。②Maginus 法：以太阳真视运动（非平运动）取度——生时与次同日同时分之太阳赤经差=一年之度量（可配通用或专属表，见《Christian Astrology》页711）。③Naibod 法（今公认最佳）：以太阳平运动为一年之度量——1°=1年5日8时；59分8秒=整年；每分≈6日4时。三法差异不巨，可随意用（某盘或某法更合）。
rules.notes: CHAP XXV 1-4；本卷实操从 Naibod 度量+Argol 相位方向法

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.original_text: The Years and Dayes of the Ark of Direction may be found according to Naibod's Measure without this table, thus; let the Ark of Direction be 16d. 18m. the Logist. Logar. thereof is [3581] from whence Substract the Logist. Logar. of 59m. 8s. (the Sun's Mean Diurnal Motion) viz. [63] and the remainder is [3519] the Logist. Log. of 26d. 41m. This 26d. Is 26 Years, and 41 min. in Ptolomy's Table gives 249 dayes, 14h. 6m.
rules.translation: Naibod 度量换算（无表算法）：方向弧之 Logist.Log. − 太阳日均平运动59分8秒之 Logist.Log. = 年数之 Logist.Log.（例：弧16°18'→Logist.3581−63=3519→26°41'=26年+41分；41分按 Ptolemy 表=249日14时6分）。
rules.notes: CHAP XXV 附；另有 Naibod 通用/专属换算表及归算表（归算恒加于方向弧：29°30'加25分=29°55'→29年11月）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.original_text: There is another Measure of Time which seems very Rational, and here I commend it to the Practice of all Curious Artists as the most excellent Measure of Time today in use... by this Method every Nativity will have something a different Measure of Time, which depends wholly upon the Motion of the Sun. The Rule to Form a Table, is thus; Take the apparent Right Ascension of the Sun from the day of the Nativity (be it more, or less than equal degrees) day by day, forward on; as thus, let the difference of R.A. the Sun from the day of Birth to ten dayes after compleat, be the Measure of Time for ten Years, &c.
rules.translation: 第四种时间度量（Coley 推为今日最优、每盘各异）：取太阳自生日起逐日之视赤经——生日至十日之赤经差=十年之度量；以此制归算表：日赤经差大于60分者其归算从方向弧减，小于60分者加（例：1645-11-9 盘，24°29′弧减2°1′=22年近6月）。Coley 谓此与开普勒取太阳黄道日行之度量相符（开普勒用黄道、此用赤经）。
rules.notes: CHAP XXV 末；Mr. J.E. 亲验称其真确最富；本卷实操仍守 Naibod+Argol

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 校正与方向须同一度量
rules.original_text: observe this as a general Rule, that whatsoever measure of time you Rectifie a Nativity by, you are to use the same measure in all Directions, but to Rectifie by one kind of measure and Direct by another is absurd.
rules.translation: 通用总则：以何种时间度量校正（Rectify）命盘，即须以同度量用于一切方向——以一度量校正、另度量推方向者为荒谬。
rules.notes: CHAP XXV 末总则；Morinus 主张校正宜用 Converse 方向

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley, with William Lilly's commendatory preface
rules.result: 事件校正最确、日月法次之
rules.original_text: [Rectification 校正之法，CHAP III 已详：事件校正最确，日月校正法（Pole of Position 试算+比例内插得真极），Hermes Trutine 受胎校正法（受胎月/日表，Haly/Ptolemy 认可，但 Coley 明言不如事件校正），及 Animodar/行运/推进等校正法并皆弃用。]
rules.translation: 校正法总纲（回指 CHAP III）：事件校正最确（Speculum 17 栏制图，dexter/sinister 相位，升点按斜升约1°/年、天顶按赤经推）；日月校正法（以 Pole of Position 试算+比例内插得真极）；Hermes Trutine 受胎校正（受胎月/日表，Haly/Ptolemy 认可，Coley 明言不如事件校正）；Animodar、行运、推进诸校正法并皆弃用。
rules.notes: 本条目为对 CHAP III（行13326-13637）之总括，供引擎方向法模块引用；详见 Part III 排盘卷 CHAP III 原文

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: This query is Answered from the consideration of the eighth House and Planets posited therein, or beholding them; when the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon shall be in good Aspect with the Lord of the eighth, or Planet therein, it shews the Querent will dye a Natural Death; the same if the Fortunes be in the eighth, or have Dignities therein, or behold the Moon by any good Aspect.
rules.translation: 问死之种类（自然/暴力）·判一：察8宫及宫内/照宫之星——问主宫主或月亮与8宫主或宫内星吉照=自然之死；吉星居8宫或于8宫有尊、或吉照月亮=同。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT I 1；Part II 问卜（与 Part III 判例卷 CP3-381 呼应）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If one of the Fortunate Planets be in the eighth House, and the other in the Ascendant, or if the Lord of eighth, the Moon, or Lord of the Ascendant be not in violent Signes, or neer violent fixed Stars, this Argues the Querent will not be subject to a violent death.
rules.translation: 问死之种类·判二（免暴死）：一吉星居8宫、另一居升点；或8宫主/月/1宫主皆不落凶暴星座、不近凶暴恒星=不受暴死之害。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT I 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 依克星之位定死法（坠/溺/铁火）
rules.original_text: But if the Luminaries are in violent Signes, not beholding each other, or if they do behold each other by Square or Opposition from Angles, or are afflicted by the Infortunes, it threatens violent death; and if Saturn or Mars happen to have Dignities in the eighth, it confirms the judgment... Now the kinds of violent Deaths are thus found; If Saturn or Mars be in the tenth House in Fiery Signes, afflicting the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant and they neer violent Fixed Stars, shews Death by some violent fall from a high place. Saturn in Cancer afflicting as aforesaid shews Drowning; and Mars, the afflicting Planet in a Fiery Signe, shews death by Iron, Fire, Sword, Gunshot, &c.
rules.translation: 问暴死·判三：日月落凶暴星座且互不相照、或自角宫刑冲、或受凶星克=暴死之危（土火于8宫有尊更验）。暴死种类：土/火居10宫火象座克月或1宫主且近凶暴恒星=高处坠亡；土居巨蟹克=溺死；火居火象座克=铁/火/刀剑/火器之死。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT I 3；'more of this in the Third Part'（即卷A CP3-385/386）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: Saturn being Lord of the eighth House, (and the death found to be Natural) signifies some tedious Ague, Dropsie or Consumption. Mars threatens Death by Wounds, or some Fiery hot Distemper, as Feavers; the Sun, by some obstructions of the Vital Spirits or Pluresie; Mercury by Phrenzy, Madness, Ptisick, Lethergie, &c. The Moon by diseases arising from Phlegm, cold and moist Humours, and sometimes Drowning.
rules.translation: 问自然死之病性：8宫主为土=久疟/水肿/痨瘵；火=刀伤/热性之疾如热病；日=元气流滞/胸膜炎；水=癫狂/疯病/肺痨/嗜睡；月=痰湿冷湿之疾、或竟溺死。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT I 4；'See more in the Judgment of the sixth House'（卷A CP3-383 同旨）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: As the Ascendant Signifies the Querent, and the second House his Substance; so the Wife is Signified by the seventh House, and her Estate by the eighth House and Lord thereof... Now if you find the Lord of the eighth strong, and the eighth house free from the presence of the Infortunes, and both well beheld by Jupiter and Venus this argues the Portion is Considerable; The same if you find Jupiter, Venus, the Dragons Head, or the Part of Fortune in the eighth House, no way afflicted... the Querent will obtain it with ease.
rules.translation: 问妻妆奁·判一（厚而易得）：8宫主强、8宫无凶星临、且俱受木金吉照=妆奁丰厚；木/金/龙头/福点居8宫无克=同；兼证=得之甚易（女问夫之产业同理）。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT II 1；妆奁/遗产同论

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If the Significators be found weak and infortunate, either Combust, Retrograde or Slow in Motion, and afflicted by the Infortunes, this argues not only a very Inconsiderable Fortune with a Wife, but great Vexation and Trouble in obtaining what there is, or a very uncomfortable enjoyment thereof.
rules.translation: 问妻妆奁·判二（薄而多烦）：征象星弱而失幸（灼/逆/缓行、受凶星克）=妆奁甚微薄，且得之过程多烦扰、纵得亦难安享。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT II 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If the Lord of the Ascendant be in Square or Opposition of the Lord of the eighth House, or if Saturn or Mars be Peregrine therein, or the Dragons Tail there, 'tis in vain for the Querent to hope for any good; for either the Portion is small and invalluable, or the Querent will be strangely Cheated thereof, or suffer much prejudice concerning the same, insomuch that he had better desist than make any progress as to the obtaining thereof.
rules.translation: 问妻妆奁·判三（无望）：1宫主刑冲8宫主；或土火游走（Peregrine）居8宫；或龙尾居8宫——盼奁无益：奁小无值、或被奇诓骗、或大受其损，宁弃之勿求。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT II 3

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
planets: 月/1宫主/4宫主/8宫主/10宫主/12宫主
rules.original_text: If in the Figure of the Question propounded you find the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant applying by any bad Aspect to the Lord of the fourth, eighth, tenth, or twelfth houses, there is great danger the Person may suffer for the fact he is Apprehended for.
rules.translation: 问被控之人受损或死·判一：月或1宫主以恶照应用于4/8/10/12宫主=其所被捕之事有大险（受刑/受损之危）。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT III 1

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant apply to the Conjunction, Square or Opposition of Saturn or Mars in bad places of the Heavens, and the fortunate Planets no way Assist by their Friendly Beams, you may then conclude the Querent is guilty of the Crime he is Charged withal, and the Case seems very dangerous on his side.
rules.translation: 问被控·判二（有罪）：月或1宫主合/刑/冲土火于天象凶位、且吉星毫不施吉照=问主实犯其所被控之罪、案情甚危。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT III 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: But if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon be with Jupiter or Venus, or in Sextile or Trine, or Reception of either of them, then the Querent speeds well, and comes off with Honour, without the least prejudice; and this the more certain, if either of the Fortunes happen to have Dignities in the tenth, eleventh, or fourth houses, and are posited in the Ascendant or Mid-heaven.
rules.translation: 问被控·判三（无罪脱身）：1宫主或月与木/金合、或六合三合、或互容=问主顺遂、光荣脱身、毫无损伤（木金于10/11/4宫有尊且居升/天顶尤验）。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT III 3

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If the Lord of the Ascendant be free from affliction, and another Planet who has any Essential Dignity therein be in bad Aspect to the Infortunes, then the Querent goes off clear, and some of his Confederates are brought into Trouble.
rules.translation: 问被控·判四（同伙受罪）：1宫主不受克、而于其内有本然尊贵之别星恶照凶星=问主清白脱身、其同伙受累入狱。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT III 4

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: In fine, If the Significators of the Querent be Essentially strong, and free from the Malicious Rayes of Saturn and Mars, and located in some good place of the Figure, then the Querent is safe, and comes off without the least Damage; notwithstanding all Fears and jealousies of Danger that otherwise might affright and perplex him.
rules.translation: 问被控·判五（总安）：问主征象本然强、无土火恶照、居图中吉位=全然安全、毫发无损——纵有种种危惧之念萦扰。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII SECT III 5

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: [Handwritten: Whether the Querent or his Wife shall dye first. Consider the Significators viz. the Lord of the Ascendant and the 7th and see which of them goes first to the Lord of the eighth by Conjunction, Square or Opposition, or the like of any Infortune, as to combustion of the Sun; that which is most powerfull and strong in all probability will live longest...]
rules.translation: 问夫妻孰先死（手写批注）：察1宫主与7宫主——视孰先以合/刑/冲行至8宫主、或先至任何凶星之恶照（如日灼）者；最强最有力者大抵最寿。
rules.notes: CHAP VIII 末手写批注（原文残缺，[ ]内为编者补）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 受克=险（土=病失/火尾=盗骗）
rules.original_text: In this Question you must have Recourse to the ninth House, and his Lord, to the Planets posited therein or beholding the said Significators, as also the Moon and Lord of the Ascendant... if you find any of the Significators impedited, or much afflicted, you may then suspect much Hazzard in the Voyage; if Saturn be the Planet afflicting, it signifies the Querent is threatened with some tedious Disease, or loss of Goods; if Mars afflict, or the Dragons Tail it portends prejudice by Thieves or Pyrates, and oftentimes Couzening and Cheating among themselves.
rules.translation: 问航海顺利否·判一（险）：察9宫其主及宫内星、照宫之星、兼月与1宫主——征象受克/大损=航程多险；土克=久病或失货之危；火或龙尾克=盗贼海盗之害、或彼此诓骗。
rules.notes: CHAP IX SECT I 1

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 强吉照=成；座定星迟=航长
rules.original_text: But if you find the Significators strong, and no way prejudiced but free, and the Lord of the Ascendant in Friendly Aspect of the Lord of the ninth, or if there be Reception between them, and the Fortunes happen to lend their Assistance, you may then conclude the Querent may make a Happy, Prosperous and successful Voyage; and by considering the Sign of the ninth, whether Fixed or Moveable, and the Significators, whether swift or slow in Motion, you may judge of the length of the Voyage.
rules.translation: 问航海·判二（吉而可成）：征象强而无损、1宫主与9宫主吉照/互容、吉星相助=航行幸福顺遂有成；航程长短视9宫座固定/动与征象星行速/行迟。
rules.notes: CHAP IX SECT I 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
planets: 1宫主/8宫主/6宫主/12宫主/4宫主/土/火
rules.original_text: Moreover, the Ascendant and the Lord thereof must be much Regarded in this Case; for if the ninth and tenth houses be well fortified, and excellently Fortunate as can be desired, yet if the Lord of the Ascendant be afflicted by the Lord of the eighth House, or otherwise, the Querent may end his dayes in the Voyage, and never Return again; or if he be afflicted by the Lord of the sixth or in the sixth House by Saturn or Mars, he may be sick in his Voyage, or Wounded; if the Lord of the twelfth afflict, Imprisonment or Restraint is to be feared; if the Lord of the fourth, the Grave may swallow him up.
rules.translation: 问航海·判三（1宫主大要）：纵9/10宫坚固吉利，仍须重察升点与其主——1宫主受8宫主克=客死航途、不复归来；受6宫主克或居6宫受土火克=途中病/伤；受12宫主克=囚禁之惧；受4宫主克=葬身鱼腹。
rules.notes: CHAP IX SECT I 3；升点与其主为问卜总键

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: In this Case observe in what part of the Scheme you find the Part of Fortune and the Dispositer thereof, or Jupiter or Venus free from affliction, or any of the Planets that are powerful in the Figure, I say, observe the Quarter of Heaven, where any of these Promising Planets are posited, and direct the Querent that way; but see that they are not posited in an obscure dejected place of the Heavens; if so, take that Planet that is next in Power, alwayes rejecting the Consideration of the places of Saturn or Mars, unless they are strong and in their Essential Dignities in good Aspect to the Fortunes or Lord of the Ascendant.
rules.translation: 问航海航向择吉方：察福点及其Dispositor、或木金（无克）、或图中有力之星所在之天区，令问主向此方航行；若落阴暗卑下之处则取次强之星；常弃土火之位——除非彼等强而本然受尊、吉照吉星或1宫主。
rules.notes: CHAP IX SECT I 4

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 吉照互容=得/刑冲有容=成而劳
rules.original_text: You are in this case to see what Aspect there is between the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon and the Lord of the ninth House, or Planets therein; & if you find they behold each other by good Aspect, or if the Moon be in the ninth, or the Lord of the Ascendant there, or if there be a friendly reception between the Significators, these are good Arguments, that the Querent may obtain his desire; the same if the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Moon be in Sextile or Trine to Jupiter or the Sun, but if the Aspect be by Square or Opposition; yet if there be Reception or Translation of Light, it argues the Business shall be accomplished, although with some Trouble and Pains.
rules.translation: 问得俸禄（Benefice）·判一：1宫主/月与9宫主（或宫内星）吉照；月居9宫；1宫主居9宫；征象互容=可得所求；1宫主或月六合三合木或日同；虽刑冲、但有互容或传光=事成而多劳烦。
rules.notes: CHAP IX SECT II 1；亦通于得学位/技艺知识

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If you find the Infortunes in the Ninth House or the Ascendant, or otherwise afflicting those houses, or their Lords, and if so be you can find none of the aforesaid Testimonies in the Figure, you may then conclude there is small hopes, and the Querent will then very rarely obtain his desire, nay there is no probability of any such thing to be procured.
rules.translation: 问得俸禄·判二（无望）：凶星居9宫或升点、或以他式克此二宫或其主、且图中全无上述吉证=希望甚微、罕得所求、殆无成事之可能。
rules.notes: CHAP IX SECT II 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: Here you are to consider how the Lord of the tenth House, & the Sun do either of them Aspect the Lord of the Ascendant, & the Moon: if they are in friendly Reception by House or Exaltation, or in Sextile or Trine of each other; if so, these are assured Testimonies that the Querent may by using means obtain the place desired; the same if you find the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon posited in the tenth House, or the Lord of the tenth, or the Sun in the Ascendant; and if they happen Friendly to behold each other also at the same time; why, then you need not question but your desire will take effect. [Note that the Advantage that may arise from the Office or Dignity desired must be considered from the strength and position of the Lord of the eleventh House.]
rules.translation: 问得位·判一（可得）：10宫主或日与1宫主/月吉照、互容（本宫或擢升）、六合三合=用其手段可得所求之位；1宫主或月居10宫、10宫主或日居升点、且互相吉照=必得。附注：所谋职位之利须察11宫主之强弱与位置。
rules.notes: CHAP X SECT I 1

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: But on the contrary, if nothing of this kind can be found in your Figure, neither the good Aspect of the Significators, translation of Light, Reception, or dwelling in Houses, this is an evident Testimony that the Querent shall not have the Place desired, notwithstanding he be never so fairly promised.
rules.translation: 问得位·判二（不得）：图中全无吉照/传光/互容/居宫诸证=问主不得所求之位——纵被再三美言许诺。
rules.notes: CHAP X SECT I 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: But if the Querent be in an Imployment, and fears he may be turned out... look to the Significators, and see if there be any good Aspect between them (as before noted) or if there be Reception, & judge accordingly, that the Querent stands sure, and needs not fear a remove from his present Imployment; and this the rather if the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Moon be in good Aspect of Jupiter or Venus in the tenth House.
rules.translation: 问去职之惧·判一（稳）：征象间有吉照或互容=职位稳固、无去职之惧；1宫主或月吉照居10宫之木金尤验。
rules.notes: CHAP X SECT II 1

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 恶照=将见逐于克星所表之人
rules.original_text: But if you find the Significator of the Querent in any bad Aspect with those Planets which are in friendly Reception, or behold the Sun or Lord of the tenth house by Sextile or Trine, you may then inform the Querent he is in danger of being outed of his place, through the means of such persons signified by the Planets that afflict the Querents Significator.
rules.translation: 问去职之惧·判二（将逐）：问主征象恶照彼等（与凶星互容者）、或六合三合照日/10宫主之星=有被逐之险——逐之者即克问主征象之星所表之人。
rules.notes: CHAP X SECT II 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: As to success in Trade from this House also... If the Significators of Trade be posited in fiery signes, you may then conclude any Profession of that Nature will best agree with the Querent; if in Earthly, Airy, Watry Signes, judge accordingly, considering the qualities and professions which the Planets naturally signifie as before directed in this Book.
rules.translation: 问贸易成败与职业相宜：贸易征象星居火象座=火属之业最宜问主；居土/风/水象座依各星本性所主之职业类推判断。
rules.notes: CHAP X SECT II 3；详见第三部分职业判法（卷A CP3-364/365）

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: The Lord of the eleventh, and the eleventh House signifie the thing in question, and if the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant be in Sextile or Trine to the Lord of the eleventh House, or any good Planet be posited therein, or if there be a Reception, or dwelling in Houses, or translation of light between the Significators, there are good Arguments the Querent shall obtain what he hopes for.
rules.translation: 问获所求·判一：11宫与其主表所问之事——月/1宫主六合三合11宫主、吉星居11宫、征象互容/居宫/传光=问主可得其所望。
rules.notes: CHAP XI SECT I 1

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 恶证=不得；指名物察对应宫主
rules.original_text: But if you find Cross Aspects between the Significators, or if they be Combust, Cadent, or Retrograde, or Saturn or Mars sends forth their malicious Rayes to the Significators; judge the contrary. This is to be understood when the thing hoped for is not Nominated; but if you understand by the Querent what it is he hopes for, then consider also the Planet and House that signifies the thing hoped for; as if the thing were Money, why then take notice of the second House, and the Lord thereof, see how the Lord of the eleventh holds that Planet, and accordingly judge.
rules.translation: 问获所求·判二（反证与指名）：征象间恶照、或灼/降/逆、或土火施恶照=不得；若问主指名所求之物（如金钱），则察表该物之星与宫（钱=2宫与2宫主）——看11宫主如何对待该星而断。
rules.notes: CHAP XI SECT I 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: What is said of Hopes, may be fitly applyed to the Querents Friends, (not related) whether they will prove real or not, if you find the Significators in good Aspect of the Moon, or Lord of the Ascendant, or Planets therein, you may judge the Friends of the Querent are Faithful, Just, and true unto him; but if you find contrary Aspects, you have reason to judge the contrary: 'tis not safe to impose Trust or Confidence in them.
rules.translation: 问友真伪：征象星吉照月/1宫主或升内之星=友忠实正直可信；恶照=反之、不可托信。
rules.notes: CHAP XI SECT I 3

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 固定角主/征象落凶宫受克=久囚
rules.original_text: Fixed Signe Ascending, and the Lord thereof Angular, especially Saturn argues a tedious Imprisonment, the same if the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Moon be in the fourth, sixth, eighth or twelfth Houses, and there afficted, or otherwise unfortunate, being Combust or Retrograde.
rules.translation: 问囚释放·判一（久囚）：固定座升、其主居角（尤土星）=久长之苦囚；1宫主或月居4/6/8/12宫受克/失幸（灼/逆）同断。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 1；附编者注：星与座示期、位置示能否实现

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 速行强于12主+木金吉照=速释
rules.original_text: But if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon be swift in motion, or if they shall be stronger than the Lord of the twelfth, to dispose of him, and in moveable Signes, and well beheld of Jupiter or Venus, these are Testimonies of a speedy Releasment.
rules.translation: 问囚释放·判二（速释）：1宫主或月行速、或强于12宫主、居动座、且受木金吉照=将速获释。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 2

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If you find the Lord of the Ascendant in any bad Aspect of the Lord of the twelfth, or Planet therein, you may thence conclude the Querent hath private Enemies and he suffers prejudice by them; or if any other Planet being Lord of some other house afflict the Moon, or Lord of the Ascendant, the Querent hath private Enemies.
rules.translation: 问暗敌·判一：1宫主恶照12宫主或12宫内星=问主有暗敌且受其害；别宫之主克月或1宫主亦然。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 3

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: But if the Significators of the Querent be in good Aspect of the fortunes, and free from all bad Aspects of the Infortunes, or any other Planet, he may then conclude, he hath no private Enemies, And by considering the position of the former Significators, you may judge if the Querent shall be infortunate in great Cattle, &c.
rules.translation: 问暗敌·判二（无）：问主征象与吉星吉照、且不受凶星或任何行星恶照=无暗敌；据上述征象之位亦可断问主于大牲畜之得失。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 4

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If a Question be demanded whether a Distempered Person be Bewitched or not... See if you find the Lord of the Ascendant in the twelfth house, in Conjunction, Square, or Opposition, with the Lord thereof, or if the Lord of the sixth be in the twelfth house, or Lord of the twelfth in the sixth in any bad Aspect to the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant, these are Arguments in Art the Party is Bewitched, or under the power of some evil Person; the same if one Planet be Lord of the Ascendant and twelfth houses, then the Disease is more than Natural.
rules.translation: 问病者是否被蛊：1宫主居12宫合/刑/冲12宫主；6宫主居12宫；12宫主居6宫恶照月或1宫主=其人被蛊或受恶人制；一星兼1/12宫主=病超乎自然。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 5

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If the Infortunes be posited in the twelfth House, weak and debilitated, or the Lord of the twelfth in the Ascendant, or the Moon in the twelfth in Conjunction, Square or Opposition of the Lord of the twelfth house, these are great Arguments, that the Disease is not only Occult, but more than Natural. [Coley's opinion:] I am sensible this is a Matter much disputed by some in these dayes... I am inclined to believe there is such a thing as Witchcraft, if the Reports and Relations of several Persons of good Credit may be confided in... But I shall not take upon me to Determine any thing positively in this dubious matter, let every one enjoy his own Opinion.
rules.translation: 问隐疾超自然：凶星弱居12宫；12宫主居升点；月居12宫合/刑/冲12宫主——皆为隐疾且超乎自然之大证；察1宫主与克星所居之宫可近猜祸源与何人。Coley 按语：此道近日多有争议，然彼信巫术实有（若目击者言可信）；于此疑案不妄断，各从其见。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 6；含 Coley 个人立场（信其有而不妄断），信仰性条目标 low

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 依小时主星宫位定名次；落陷克=坠/折/死
rules.original_text: When it shall be demanded which of the two Beasts that are to Run a Race shall Win... regard the Lord of the Hour in which the Question is propounded, and if thou findest him in the Horoscope, the Querents Horse... shall win; but if the Lord of the Hour shall be in the Mid-heaven, say that he shall be the second from the first, and if he be in the eleventh or third house, say the same: But if he be in the seventh House, say he will be between the first and the last; and if in the fourth House, say he will be the last of all; if the Lord of the Hour shall be in his Fall, the Rider shall be fearful, and not only fearful, but in danger of falling from his Horse; and if the Infortunate Planets shall cast any Aspect unto him (chiefly from bad places of the Figure) he will go neer to break some of his Limbs, and the hurt will be in that Member represented by that Signe in which the Significator is posited: But if the Aspect of the Infortune be an Opposition, the Rider will be in danger of Death...
rules.translation: 问赛马胜负（依 Haly《De Judic. Astrorum》）：察问时之小时主星——居升点=问主之马（或所问之马）胜；居天顶=第二名；居11/3宫=第三名；居7宫=首末之间；居4宫=最后。小时主星落陷=骑者恐惧、且恐坠马；凶星照之（尤自凶位）=将折肢、伤在征象星所落星座所表之肢体；凶照为冲=骑者有死险（其伤肢之宫主星失幸且月失幸尤重）。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 末 Haly 引；赛马问卜为赌博性占断，仅规则引擎研究收录，不作现实用途

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
signs: 擢升/落陷/本宫/三体/界/面
rules.original_text: But if the Querent have not his Beast in the Race, and inquire which Horse shall win the Race, behold the Lord of the Hour, and if you find him in the Ascendant, Mid-heaven, or eleventh Houses, say that Horse shall win the Race, that is of that colour of that Planet as shall be posited in any of the aforesaid places; and if the Significator of the Winning Horse shall be in his Exaltation House, or Triplicity, he shall be the more Remarkably known and discovered... if in this we find him in his fall, the Horse is unlucky, ill favoured, and of evil qualities; but if he be in his Exaltation or House, he will be singularly famous in himself; if in his Triplicity, he is noted all over the Countrey, but not very excellent in himself; if in his Terme or Decanate, he is known... If the Age of the Horse be enquired of, consider the Significators position, whether he be Oriental, then he is young; if Occidental, he is old; if he be in the North Angle, he is very old.
rules.translation: 问赛马（马不在赛而问谁胜）：察小时主星——居升点/天顶/11宫=具该行星颜色之马（居上述位者）胜；胜马征象在擢升/本宫/三体=显著知名（擢升尤甚）；落陷=劣马、貌丑质劣；居擢升或本宫=独擅盛名；居三体=举国知名而非绝伦；居界/面=知名而已。问马龄：征象东方=少壮、西方=老、居北角=甚老。
rules.notes: CHAP XII 末 Haly 引续；赌博性占断，仅规则引擎研究收录

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 月依合序断六问，星强位佳=吉
rules.original_text: Many people will usually come to the Astrologer indiscreetly, asking many things of him... wherefore when you have not the Ascendant Contracted to the Question, take the more general thing for the Querent, which is the Moon, and the other Planets shall signifie the things quesited... for if they are six, or less, judge of them according to the Conjunction the Moon makes with the other six Planets; and you may know the Nature of the Question, by the nature of the Planet to whom the Moon is first joyned after the Question proposed, and observe the disposition of the Planet, and accordingly judge of the effect of that thing; for if he be strong, and well placed, free from Impediments, judge the effect of it will be good, if ill posited, judge the contrary. Then see to what Planet the Moon is next joyned after her separation from that Planet, and according to his disposition judge of the second thing; then observe the next Application from that separation, and judge accordingly for the six Questions, and give the same judgment of an Aspect as of a Corporal Conjunction.
rules.translation: 多问同判法（依 Guido Bonatus）·判一：多人并提多问而无专宫可依时——以月亮为问主通征、余六星表所问诸事；问数六或以下：依问后月亮与六星相合之次第断之，月首合之星表首问（行星之性示问之性质）、察该星之配置判其成败（强而有位无碍=吉、位恶=凶）；次察月离该星后再合之次星断第二问，逐问类推；成相与体合同判。
rules.notes: 行7907 起 Guido Bonatus 引；无专宫可依时的总法

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: And if your questions exceed six, then afterwards judge by the Lords of the Triplicities of the Houses in which the Planets are when the Moon is joyned to them by Body or Aspect. As for Example, if the Moon be joyned to Mars in her first Conjunction... and Mars be in Virgo, then when thou hast compleated the first six questions... then judge of the seventh question according to the Ruler of the first Triplicity of Virgo, which is Venus... and also judge of the eighth according to the Lord of the first Triplicity of Cancer, which is Mars; and thus to the twelve questions; and if the questions be more, judge by the three Lords of the Triplicities, as by the first and second; and if the questions exceed this number, then judge by the Lords of the Angles; and if they exceed still, then judge by the Lords of the Triplicities of the Angles.
rules.translation: 多问同判法·判二（七问以上）：问过六问——第七问起按行星所居宫之三分主判（例：月首合处女之火星，七问按处女第一三分主金星、八问按巨蟹第一三分主火星……至十二问）；问更多则依三分诸主（第一第二递补）、再依角宫之主、再依角宫三分主，逐级递推。
rules.notes: 行7930 起；三级递补判法

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 依强征象之位断成否真伪
rules.original_text: But if the question be concerning any thing, whether it be true or false; or concerning two or three things, which is better to take than the other; or whether News or Rumors be true or false, judge as is usually directed in the ninth, tenth, and eleventh houses. For if any one ask concerning many things, which is best for him, or most profitable; or concerning Rumors... behold the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon, and see which of them is strongest, and by him operate; and if the stronger of them be in an Angle, free from Impediment, and in Reception, the thing first named will be best and most true, and fittest for the Querent, and best obtained: But if the Lord of the first or the Moon be impedited, there will be some mention of the thing, but afterwards it will come to nothing; yet if the Lord of the first or the Moon behold the first, and be received in a succedent House, or free from Impediments, the Querent shall obtain the thing quesited; and if they be impedited, it will be lost after 'tis obtained; and if he be in a Cadent House, free from other Impediments and received, the Querent shall obtain the thing quesited; or it is true if it be concerning any News or Rumors: But if the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon be Impedited in a Cadent House, whatever the Question is it will come to nothing.
rules.translation: 多问同判法·判三（真伪/择优/流言）：真伪或择优之问依9/10/11宫常法断；多事择优——取1宫主与月之强者操断：强者居角无碍且受容=首提之事最善最真最宜、最易得；1宫主或月受碍=事有提及而后无成；居续宫受容无碍=得之（受碍则得而复失）；居降宫受容无碍=得之、若为流言则真；居降宫受碍=无论何问皆归无成。
rules.notes: 行7947 起；角/续/降三态判法

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.original_text: If several persons come together, & propound Questions to the Artist, let him take the Ascendant for the first person that propounds, and the second house shall be the Ascendant of the second person, and the third house the Ascendant of the third person, &c. and so vary all the rest accordingly; but the surest way is for every person to go to an Artist single without other Company that would be Querents also. Here ends the Rules how to judge the several Questions appertaining to the the Twelve Houses of Heaven.
rules.translation: 多问同判法·判四（多人同来）：多人并问——升点为第一问者、2宫为第二人之升点、3宫为第三人……依次轮转；然最稳之法为各人独往、勿与他人同问。至此十二宫问卜诸规则完结。
rules.notes: 行7969 起；Part II 问卜规则之收束

rules.book: Clavis Astrologiae Elimata (1676, 2nd ed.), Henry Coley
rules.result: 诸星Testimonies：土17/木4弱/火13/日11/金13/水12弱/月1弱
rules.original_text: CHAP. XI. CONTAINS ONLY A SPECULUM OF THE NATIVITY, AND THE DIGNITIES AND DEBILITIES OF THE PLANETS, &C. A Speculum of the Geniture, or Table of the Radiations of the Planets. [Table] A Table of the Fortitudes and Debilities of the Planets in the Geniture, both Essential and Accidental. Hence it appears that, Saturn is strong by 17 Testimonies; Jupiter weak by 4; Mars strong by 13; The Sun strong by 11; Venus strong by 13; Mercury weak by 12; The Moon weak by 1.
rules.translation: CHAP XI（全章仅含本命 Speculum 表与诸星尊卑表）：Speculum=本命盘行星光行辐射总表（1650 盘17栏版式）；行星 Fortitudes/Debilities 表（本然+偶发尊贵/衰弱）。判例盘诸星强弱 Testimonies：土强17、木弱4、火强13、日强11、金强13、水弱12、月弱1。
rules.notes: 行17269-17280；Speculum 17栏与尊卑表为判例盘之总览（原表为版式，txt 仅提取文字）；此表即引擎'行星强弱计算'之权威验证基准——1650 盘各星尊贵衰弱计数（对照映射T）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: For Saturn which is the highest of them all, and hath [the] greatest circle, finishes not his course of revolution but in 30 years, Jupiter in 12 years, Mars in 2 years, the Sun in 365 days & about 6 hours, Venus and Mercury keep their course like the Sun: the Moon maketh her revolution in 27 days, and about eight hours.
rules.translation: 行星周期：土 30 年、木 12 年、火 2 年、日 365 日 6 时、金水同日、月 27 日 8 时。

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: Saturn is cold and dry, melancholic, an enemy and destroyer of the nature and life of man, of the day, masculine, evil, and the greatest misfortune. Jupiter is hot and moist, sanguine, a friend and preserver of the life and nature of man, masculine, of the day, and is called the greatest fortune. Mars is immoderately hot & dry, choleric, masculine, and of the night, evil, and the lesser misfortune. The Sun is moderately hot and dry, masculine, and of the day, fortunate by aspect, infortunate by corporal conjunction. Venus is cold and moist, temperate, phlegmatic, feminine, of the night, of good nature, and is called the lesser fortune. Mercury in all things is common and mutable, he is good with the good, and evil with the evil... The Moon is likewise cold and moist... she doth change her nature and quality according to the quarters.
rules.translation: 行星性质表：土=冷干忧郁、昼/阳/凶/最大凶；木=热湿血性、昼/阳/吉/最大吉；火=过热干胆汁、夜/阳/凶/次凶；日=中热干、昼/阳/照吉合凶；金=冷湿温和、夜/阴/吉/次吉；水=全变、随伴星；月=冷湿、依象限变化。
rules.notes: 日：'fortunate by aspect, infortunate by corporal conjunction'

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The head of the Dragon is in all points like to Mercury, good with the good planets, and evil with the evil planets: for being joined with the good planets, he doth increase their goodness, and with the evil their malice. The tail of the Dragon is contrary to the head, for he is evil with the good and good with the evil.
rules.translation: 龙首=水星性（随伴星增减吉凶）；龙尾相反（与吉星合则减吉、与凶星合则减凶）。
rules.notes: 龙尾=龙首对宫

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: These be in number five, that is: the house, the exaltation, the triplicity, the term, and the face... Unto this dignity because it is the first and chiefest is attributed the number of five... The second essential dignity... hath given unto him the number of four... the triplicity hath the third place... has for his value, three in number... And unto this dignity [the term] is attributed and given the number [two]... This dignity [the face] is the least of all, and hath given unto it the number of one.
rules.translation: 五尊贵计分：庙 5 分、擢 4 分、三分 3 分、界 2 分、面 1 分（阶序与分值，供 almuten 计算）。
rules.notes: 与 Lilly 系 5/4/3/2/1 同源；反对宫=失势（detriment）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The Sun and the Moon... are allotted for that cause for their houses two signs agreeable to their natures... the Lion for the Sun, and the Crab for the Moon... the other five have two signs... That is to say, the day house shall be in a diurnal sign, and the night house in a nocturnal sign. Then Saturn... hath he obtained for his houses... Capricorn and Aquarius, of the which Capricorn is the night house, and Aquarius the day house. Jupiter... hath for his houses Sagittarius and Pisces... Sagittarius is the day house and Pisces the night. Mars following after has for his houses Aries and the Scorpion, whereof Aries is the day house, and Scorpio the night... Venus... Taurus and Libra: of the which, Taurus is the night house, and Libra the day house. Mercury... hath for his day house Gemini, and Virgo for his night house.
rules.translation: 庙宫分配：日=狮、月=蟹；土=摩羯(夜)/水瓶(昼)；木=射手(昼)/双鱼(夜)；火=白羊(昼)/天蝎(夜)；金=金牛(夜)/天秤(昼)；水=双子(昼)/处女(夜)。
rules.notes: 日/月各一庙；五星昼庙在昼宫、夜庙在夜宫；昼行星在昼庙力强于夜庙

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: the Sun, who according to the judgement of Ptolemy is exalted in Aries, but chiefly... in the 19th degree of the same... Saturn [is] thrown down and abased in the 19th degree of Aries... Jupiter is exalted in the 15 degree of the Crab, and abased in the like degree of Capricorn, and Mars is exalted in the 28 degree of Capricorn, and abased in the like degree of the Crab. Venus hath her exaltation in the 27 degree of Pisces, and in the like degree of Virgo her fall. Mercury hath his fall in the 15 degree of Pisces, and his exaltation in the like degree of Virgo. Finally, the Moon is exalted in the 3rd degree of Taurus, and abased in the like degree of Scorpio. The head... exalted in the 3rd degree of Gemini, and the tail in the 3rd of Sagittarius.
rules.translation: 擢升落陷表：日擢白羊19（陷天秤19）；月擢金牛3（陷天蝎3）；土擢天秤（陷白羊19）；木擢巨蟹15（陷摩羯15）；火擢摩羯28（陷巨蟹28）；金擢双鱼27（陷处女27）；水擢处女15（陷双鱼15）；龙首擢双子3、龙尾擢射手3。整星座取擢升（Ptolemy 系）。
rules.notes: 土擢具体度数为天秤21（如 Dorotheus 卷一）；此处从 Ptolemy 整星座

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The first, which is called the fiery triplicity, is ruled and governed by the Sun by day, by Jupiter by night, and both day and night by Saturn... The second, which is the earthly triplicity, is likewise ruled by Venus in the day, by the Moon in the night, and both by day and by night by Mars. Saturn, Mercury, and Jupiter, are lords of the third triplicity, which is of the air, but the day is subject unto Saturn, the night to Mercury, and both day and night to Jupiter. Finally the watery triplicity... hath for their lords, Venus, Mars and the Moon. Venus governor for the day, Mars for the night, and the Moon both for day and night.
rules.translation: 三分主表：火象=日(昼)/木(夜)/土(共)；土象=金(昼)/月(夜)/火(共)；气象=土(昼)/水(夜)/木(共)；水象=金(昼)/火(夜)/月(共)。
rules.notes: 每个三分为三主：昼主/夜主/共同主

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: (Table of the Egyptian terms: the first six degrees of Aries they give unto Jupiter for his term or bounds, the six degrees next following of the same sign to Venus, and the eight degrees next ensuing unto Mercury, the other ten which remain they divide into two equal parts, giving the first five unto Mars and the other five unto Saturn...)
rules.translation: 埃及界表：每星座 30° 按五段分属五星（白羊=木6/金6/水8/火5/土5，余宫见映射表）；界=行星限定作用的度数区间。
rules.notes: 重建依据：OCR 行星符号列错乱但累计度数 6/12/20/25/30 等 12 宫全部吻合标准埃及界表

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The two lights have no certain degrees for their terms or bounds, but each of them bath the one moiety or half of the Zodiac... the Sun bath for his moiety or half that part which beginneth at the first degree of the Lion, unto the last degree of Capricorn. The other moiety which beginneth at the first degree of Aquarius, and continueth to the end of the Crab, is appointed for the terms and bounds of the Moon.
rules.translation: 光体界（替代界）：日辖狮子首度至摩羯末（半黄道）；月辖水瓶首度至巨蟹末。二光处于其半年界内=等同界尊贵。

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: we will divide those 30 degrees into three equal parts, which we call faces, so that every face shall contain ten degrees... As Mars hath the first face of Aries, the Sun the second, and Venus the third. The first face of Taurus is subject to Mercury, the second to the Moon, the third to Saturn. The first face of Gemini to Jupiter, the second to Mars, the third to the Sun: and so consequently proceeding according to the order of the faces and of the planets.
rules.translation: 面：每星座三面各 10°；面主按迦勒底序（土木火日金水月）轮转：白羊=火/日/金、金牛=水/月/土、双子=木/火/日……
rules.notes: 每宫三面主=Chaldean 序推进；此尊贵分值 1

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: some are called masculine... some are called light or bright, some dark, some smoky, and some void... some are called deep... the light make these planets which are in them fortunate: the smoky, dark, and deep degrees work the contrary, the void make them neither fortunate neither unfortunate. Those which do augment fortune, are in places where there be stars of the nature of the fortunate planets... Finally, there are some degrees which are said to bring detriment, imbecility or diminution unto our bodies [azimene degrees]... when... the moon or the principal significator shall be found in any of those degrees, if they be not in one of the angles, or in his house or exaltation and oriental, it shall bring... the loss or decay of some one member, or at the least the loss of the thing that he demanded or seeketh.
rules.translation: 度性质分类：阳/阴、亮/暗/烟/空、深、增运（吉星性质星所在/吉星擢界处）、减运、azimene（凶性恒星所在）。月或主要征象星落 azimene 度且不在角/庙/擢/东出→肢体或所求之损。
rules.notes: azimene 度表在原书附表中，OCR 未能完整重建

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The Babylonians and their followers have given the dominion and rule of these hours unto the two lights, and the other planets, giving unto Saturn which is highest above the rest, the rule and dominion of the first temporal hour of the Saturday, the second to Jupiter, the third to Mars, the fourth to the Sun, the fifth to Venus, the sixth to Mercury, the seventh to the Moon, the eighth to Saturn again, and so in order according to the circle of the planets, until you come to 24 hours... the 25th hour which is the first hour of the day following is governed by the 4th planet... which is the Sun... lord of the first hour of the Sunday.
rules.translation: 行星时：迦勒底序（土木火日金水月）轮流司掌不等时；周六首时=土星，次第轮转，次日首时主=当日起始行星（周日=日）。
rules.notes: 不等时=昼夜各 12 等分；行星时=行星之尊严（卜卦时主）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: we will show that there is five sorts of them, that is to say, a conjunction, a sextile, trine, quadrate or quartile, and opposition... Some of them are aspects of amity, or love, as the trine and sextile: others of enmity and hatred, as the quadrate and opposition, the conjunction is doubtful, for with the good planet she is good, and with the evil contrary... The sextile aspect is when the centres of the two planets are distant... by the sixth part of the zodiac... 60 degrees... The quadrate... 90 degrees... The trine aspect containing the third part of the said circle, which is 120 degrees, is called the aspect of perfect amity... The opposition happeneth when the moiety or half of the zodiac containing 6 signs, or 180 degrees...
rules.translation: 相位定义：合（0°）、六合（60°=不完美友谊）、四分（90°=不完美敌意）、三合（120°=完美友谊）、对分（180°=完美敌意）；合相吉凶随伴星。
rules.notes: Firmicus：六合/四分/三合分左右（dexter=后、sinister=前）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: For Saturn casteth his beams circularly, nine degrees forward, and so much backward... The radial circle to Jupiter is of the same quality and bigness. But the circle of Mars containeth in his diameter only 16 degrees... The Sun casteth his beams in compass 15 degrees upon every part... Venus and Mercury casteth their circular beams 7 degrees every way in length... Finally the Moon sendeth forth her beams on every side 12 degrees.
rules.translation: 光束半径（应用容许度）：土 9°、木 9°、火 8°、日 15°、金 7°、水 7°、月 12°（全径翻倍）。

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The application happeneth when the circles or beams of the planets come to join together by a corporeal conjunction, or by aspect of the one half of their diameters, or when one planet is distant six degrees from a true aspect to another... the inferior planets do apply unto the superior or higher, and likewise separate themselves from them, and not contrariwise... The separation... is when one planet doth leave or depart from the aspect of another, or from his conjunction by the space of one only degree, and always he is still said to be separated until that he hath wholly left and is departed from the beams of the other.
rules.translation: 应用/分离：应用=合相或入光束半径（六合例 49.5°-54°）；分离=离 1° 起算、至出光束为止；轻（快）星向重（慢）星应用/分离，重星不反向。
rules.notes: 月离木合 1°=已分离；离 10°30′=完全分离

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: the first that cometh in place is called the prohibition, let or defence: which is that which doth let and hinder the conjunctions and aspects of the planets: which happeneth after three sorts or ways: by the body, by aspect, or by retrogradation or going backwards... as Mercury while corporally applying to the Sun, should become retrograde before he were joined to him: and this let is properly called a refranation, or holding back.
rules.translation: 阻止（禁止）：第三方以身体（居更近合点）/相位（光束更近）/逆行（refranation 阻止=先逆行而未及合）阻断两星之合或相位。
rules.notes: 例：日在金牛1°时以身体阻止火(摩羯1°)照金

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The translation of the light and nature of the planets happeneth in two sorts. First, when a light planet doth separate himself from the conjunction or aspect of another heavier than he, and afterward applyeth himself again to another that is more heavy... as Mercury, separating himself from the Sun and applying to Venus, doth transport the light and virtue of the Sun unto her. Secondly... when a light planet doth join himself... unto one that is heavier than he, and the same again to one that is more heavy. For then the second doth transport the light or nature of the first unto the third.
rules.translation: 光线传递：轻星自重星（A）分离后再应用于另一重星（B）→把 A 之光与力带给 B；或轻星合于较其重之星、此星再合更重之星→后者传递前者之光。
rules.notes: 重量序：土>木>火>日>金>水>月

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The strong reception is when a planet doth apply to the lord of a house, or exaltation, or triplicity from the place where he is, and that likewise he hath some dignity in the place where the lord is placed, and if both be in dignities one of another, having also dignity in the place where they are, and that their application be by a trine or sextile aspect, the reception shall be the better and the more perfect... but when this application is, the planets being in the lesser dignities as in their terms or faces, then their reception is weak and impotent.
rules.translation: 接收：强=双方互有尊贵（庙/擢/三分级）且三六合相位应用；弱=仅界/面级尊贵。
rules.notes: 例：月(巨蟹)六合照金(金牛)——月收金于擢、金收月于三分

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The rendering up of the virtue, is when a planet, being in his own house, or in any other of his dignities, beholdeth another which is combust or retrograde: for that planet, because of his imbecility... cannot hold or keep the virtue which the other doth communicate or give unto him by his aspect... The yielding or rendering up of the light is, when two planets which do not behold one another with any aspect, yet both of them do behold some other planet: for that planet doth gather their lights and doth cast it back again... If it happen the third planet to be more weighty than the other two, that shall be called a collection or gathering together of the lights.
rules.translation: 交还：无力之星（燃烧/逆行）接吉星之照不能持守而交还其力；光之交还=两不相照之星共照第三方（重者）=光线聚集。
rules.notes: 吉凶分级：双方角/续宫吉=利；交还者在角=利，否则不利

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: This contrariety happeneth, when a weighty planet is placed in the middle, between two light planets; the first applying unto the weighty planet, and the third, being retrograde, joineth himself to the second, and after to the first. For not only the conjunction of the first and second is letted, but also the third is joined with the second, and the first.
rules.translation: 相反性：重星居中、前星向其应用、后星逆行先合中星再合前星——不但阻断前中二星之合，且后星与前星亦相连。
rules.notes: 例：金逆合日再合水，阻断日水之合

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: This cutting of the light doth but little differ from the contrariety... first, when a third planet going forward by certain degrees into another sign, where the first and second planets are retrograde, joineth himself to the second, and not to the first... The second sort is when a planet going to the conjunction of another more weightier than he, and the same do behold another planet that is more weighty before the first be joined unto him. In this case the third planet, by his aspect, doth let the conjunction of the first and second.
rules.translation: 切断光线：第三星前行入新星座合第二星而不合第一（二者逆行）→断其传递；或行星向较重星合相时，该重星先照更重之星而阻断前者之合。
rules.notes: 例：水星向日合相时，日正四分照木，木阻水日之合

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: When any planet is hidden under the beams of the Sun, so that we cannot see it, then it is said to be combust or burnt and so is still called until it hath left the body of the Sun, by the space of 15 degrees or at the least 12.
rules.translation: 燃烧：行星藏于日芒下不可见=combust；脱离须距日 15°（至少 12°）以上。
rules.notes: 日芒下之星不参与助吉助凶（Ptolemy 同）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The almugea of the planets is no other thing but a vision or beholding of face to face in respect of the two lights, for it happeneth, when as between a planet and the Sun or the Moon there is so many signs, as there is between the house of the planet and the house of the Sun or of the Moon: so that the said planet be occidental from the Sun or oriental from the Moon.
rules.translation: Almugea（对光相见）：行星与日/月相距之星座数=其庙宫与光体庙宫相距数（行星须日落/月东出）——如日处女、金射手=almugea（金牛至狮=2宫，处女至射手=2宫）。
rules.notes: 东方=夜先日出、昼先日落；西方反之

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: the first is when any of them is void or without course or motion which is said to be when one planet separating himself from another doth not apply to any other during the time that he tarryeth in that sign... That planet which is placed out of all his dignities is called peregrine or strange. When a planet is in a sign alone by himself, and no other planet doth behold the same sign, that planet is called wild or savage. The planets are also said to be in their hayz... when the masculine planets are in masculine signs, and the diurnal or day planets are by day above the earth, and in masculine signs and degrees.
rules.translation: 状态判定：空亡=离一星后在星座内不再应用他星；游离（peregrine）=无任何尊贵；wild=独居星座无星照；hayz=阳行星在阳座且昼星昼在地上（阴反之）。
rules.notes: 月空亡为卜卦关键否词

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The planets then are most strong and fortunate, when they are in the angles or succeeding houses, or when they behold the ascendant, or else when they are in their essential dignities, or in signs of their own natures, or in the houses wherein they do rejoice. As when Mercury is in the first house, the Moon in the third, Venus in the fifth; Mars in the sixth, the Sun in the ninth, Jupiter in the eleventh, and Saturn in the twelfth. Likewise when they are in the part of their excenters furthest distant from the earth, the which is called their Aux or increase... also when they are septentrional ascendant. The masculine planets are also fortunate in the masculine degrees, and quarter of the heaven... oriental from the Sun... The force of the diurnal planets is advanced when they are by day above the earth... Likewise when their motion is increased, or they be direct, or at the least in their second station... when they are in a sextile, trine or at the least in a quartile aspect of good planets, as also when they are in the same degree and minute that the Sun is... and when they depart from combustion or from under the beams of the Sun. Finally, they are strong and fortunate when they are free and without any aspect of the malign planets, or when they are in reception with the good.
rules.translation: 偶然吉条件（综合）：角/续宫；照升点；五尊贵；本性质星座；喜乐宫（水1/月3/金5/火6/日9/木11/土12）；远地点（aux）；北纬；阳行星在阳度/阳象限/东出；昼星昼上、夜星夜上；顺行或二留；与吉星六/三/四分；与日同度（cazimi）；脱离燃烧；无凶星相位；与吉星成接收。
rules.notes: 喜乐宫同 DART-30

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The planets are called unfortunate when they are in falling houses, or that they do not behold the ascendant, and that they are out of their own essential dignities, or being in the dignities of the malign planets, as in the terms of Mars or Saturn; or that they be in their falls, or in contrary signs to their own houses, or else be retrograde or in their first station or meridional specially ascendant... or that they be slow in their motions, or joined to the tail of the Dragon... when they are besieged, that is to say, when a good planet is placed between two evil... So long also as they are combust... or that they have their course in Via Combusta, that is, in the burnt way, which is from the 13th degree of Libra, unto the 9th degree of Scorpio... They also receive great misfortune and hurt by the quadrate aspect of the evil planets, but specially by the conjunction and opposition. Likewise their strength is much weakened by the quadrate and opposition of the Sun. They suffer in like manner detriment and hurt when the evil planets are exalted above the good, or the good do apply unto the evil being retrograde.
rules.translation: 偶然凶条件（综合）：果宫；不照升点；无尊贵；居凶星之界（火/土界）；落陷；对宫（失势）；逆行或一留/南纬；慢行；合龙尾；被围困（吉星夹两凶之间）；燃烧；Via Combusta（天秤 13°-天蝎 9°）；凶星四分（尤合/冲）；日之四分/对分；吉星被凶星擢越；吉星向逆行凶星应用。
rules.notes: Via Combusta 区间=天秤13°~天蝎9°（含天蝎全段部分）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: When the Moon is increasing in her light, or number, or motion, or her course be not void or empty, she is strong and fortunate.
rules.translation: 月吉：增光/增数/增速、非空亡=强而吉。

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The Moon being void of course and she diminished in her motion and light is infortunate. When as also she bath her course through the sign of Gemini, which is the 12th sign from Cancer which is her house, or that she doth not behold Cancer, or is in the first or 12th houses, she is likewise afflicted and hurt. Also when she suffereth an Eclipse, or being in her increase hath her course with Mars, or in her decrease with Saturn, or doth not behold the place of her conjunction or opposition, immediately going before from the place that she is in, she is likewise infortunate.
rules.translation: 月凶：空亡、减速减光、行经双子（蟹之12宫=失势宫）、不照巨蟹、居一/十二宫、受蚀、增光时合火/减光时合土、不照前次合/冲点。
rules.notes: 月之失势宫=双子（巨蟹之12宫）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: following only John Regiomontanus will divide the houses by four circles, which shall pass by intersections or cuttings asunder of the meridian and horizon, and divide the heaven into 12 unequal parts, which are called houses... the four degrees of the ecliptic line, the which doth touch the meridian as well at midday as at midnight, and the horizon as well at the rising as setting. These principal degrees are the cusps or beginnings of the first, fourth, seventh and tenth houses.
rules.translation: 宫位制：Regiomontanus 四圈分宫（地平与子午线交点=角宫尖轴：1/4/7/10 宫）；四角+四续+四果。
rules.notes: 'the distance of all which houses are equal in the quarter'（每象限三等分）

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The 1st house is called the joy of Mercury, the 3rd of the Moon, the 5th of Venus the 6th of Mars, the 9th of the Sun, the 11th of Jupiter, the 12th of Saturn.
rules.translation: 行星喜乐宫：水星=1宫、月=3宫、金=5宫、火=6宫、日=9宫、木=11宫、土=12宫。
rules.notes: 与 Lilly 系一致

rules.book: A Brief and Most Easie Introduction to the Astrologicall Judgement of the Starres（卜卦总纲）
rules.author: Claudius Dariot（法国博恩医生；拉丁原文 1557《Ad Astrorum Judicia Facilis Introductio》、法文 1558、Fabian Wither 英译 1583）
rules.original_text: The first house... signifieth the life and body of him that is born or that doth ask the question... The second is the house of substance, riches or servants, and therefore is called Hope. The third house showeth us all things touching brethren, sisters, cousins, changes, small journeys, kindred, faith and religion... By the fourth... we judge of fathers, houses, lands, and ancient heritages... hidden treasures... The fifth is named the house of children... of them, of love, of ambassadors and messengers, and of gifts. The sixth house doth signify infirmities and sickness, servants and maids... small beasts and cattle... The seventh house is the house of marriage, women, contentions, wars, public enemies, banishments, robberies... buying and selling, and of runaways. This [eighth] house is the signifier of death, labours, sadness and heaviness, heritage of dead men... By the ninth house, religion, faith, visions, wisdom... dreams... long journeys... This tenth is a royal house: for by this we learn to judge of empire and rule, dignities, offices, arts, mothers, and of all things that are stolen... The eleventh house is the house of hope, trust and confidence, of footmen, of the aid and help of the king... praise and commendation. This twelfth house which is called the evil spirit, giveth... judgment of private and secret enemies, deceivers, envious persons, imprisonments, evil thoughts, whisperings, great beasts and cattle...
